links.note: What arrives 'umad ghumad chahun dish se' -- the clouds, which is 32347's own line. 32346 loses: the arrival Meera only hears a faint hint of is Hari's; this asks what literally comes from all four sides.
Word-gloss of 'daamin' = bijli, the second half of 32347's line, which its description glosses in exactly those words. 32348 loses: lightning has no part in the drizzle-and-breeze close.
Word-gloss of 'mehaa' = barsaat, lifted from 'nanhin nanhin boondan mehaa barse', 32348's own line. 32347 loses: its rain word is the 'jhar' beside the lightning, not mehaa.

Whom Meera addresses in 'baso mere nainan mein Nandlal' -- Shri Krishna. 32341's description names this as the lesson's own first question. 32342 loses: it covers the form she then describes, not the person she petitions.

All four options are months, so the tested fact is Sawan, named in 32345's opening line together with her gladness -- the lesson's third and fourth questions, which 32345 holds. 32346 loses: the bhanak is the cause of the joy, not the month.

In which bhaav she worships her aaraadhya -- bhakti bhaav, i.e. the pad's main subject prem-and-bhakti that 32341 pins to the lesson's second question. 32344 loses: its 'bhakt vachhal' line states the Lord's quality, not the devotee's bhaav.

'Giridhar' in 'Meera ke prabhu Giridhar Nagar' = Krishna, and that chhaap closes pad 2, which 32348 carries. 32344 loses: it holds pad 1's chhaap ('santan sukhdaai, bhakt vachhal Gopal'), a different closing line.

What Meera hears in Sawan -- the bhanak of Krishna's coming, 32346's own line. 32347 loses: thunder and the crack of lightning are offered as distractors here, and the key is the bhanak, not a weather sound.
Who is to dwell in Meera's eyes -- Nandlal, the vocative of the opening vinti. 32342 loses: it describes what that form looks like, not who is asked in.
Nandlal's moorat is mohani and saanvari -- 32342's line 'mohini moorati saanvari soorati' verbatim. 32343 loses: the murli and maala come after the face in the same description.
What is seated on his adhar -- the murli of 'adhar sudha ras murli raajati'. 32344 loses: its ornaments hang at the waist and the feet, not the lips.
Which maala adorns his ur/hriday -- vaijayanti, the second half of 32343's line. 32344 loses: it holds the ghantika and the noopur, nothing on the chest.
What kind her prabhu is -- 'santan sukhdaai, bhakt vachhal', pad 1's closing chhaap which 32344 carries. 32348 loses: its chhaap is pad 2's Giridhar Nagar line.

Which month's badariya is raining -- Sawan, from 'barse badariya Sawan ki', 32345's opening line. 32346 loses: it is the month's effect on her mind, while this asks the month itself. (Option key stars B Vaishakh although the correct value Sawan is option C.)
How the Sawan badariya seems -- 'man bhaavan', the very phrase of 32345's line, which names the season and its effect in one breath. 32346 loses: the umang and its cause arrive in the next line.
What comes umad-ghumad from all four directions -- the clouds, 32347's line. 32348 loses: its cool breeze is offered here as a wrong option, a separate and later image.
How the drops fall -- 'nanhin-nanhin', 32348's own line. 32347 loses: its 'jhar laavan' is the sheet of rain beside the lightning, not the size of the drops.
What the pavan is like -- 'sheetal ... sohaavan', 32348's own line. 32347 loses: there is no wind in it at all, only gathering cloud and lightning.
Krishna's eyes are vishaal/bade -- 'naina bane vishaal', 32342's line. 32341 loses: the eyes in that concept are Meera's own, the dwelling she offers, not his.
Cloze on 'adhar sudha ras ___ raajati, ur vaijanti maal' -- the missing word is murli, 32343's line. 32344 loses: a separate cloze in this same set fills noopur from its line.
Cloze on 'umad ghumad chahun dish se aaya, ___ dam kai jhar laavan ki' -- daamin, 32347's line. 32348 loses: its own cloze in this set fills sohaavan.
Cloze on 'kshudra ghantika katitat sobhit, ___ shabd rasaal' -- noopur, 32344's line. 32343 loses: its share of the description stops at the chest with the vaijayanti maala.
Cloze on 'nanhin nanhin boondan mehaa barse, sheetal pavan ___ ki' -- sohaavan, 32348's line. 32347 loses: its line ends at 'jhar laavan ki', a different refrain word.
Cloze on 'Meera ke prabhu Giridhar Nagar, ___ gaavan ki' -- aanand mangal, pad 2's chhaap which 32348 carries. 32344 loses: it holds pad 1's chhaap, filled by a different cloze in this set.
Cloze on 'Meera ke ___ santan sukhdaai, bhakt vachhal Gopal' -- prabhu, and that chhaap line of pad 1 sits in 32344. 32348 loses: pad 2's chhaap is the Giridhar Nagar line, a separate cloze here.
Cloze on 'mohini moorati saanvari soorati, naina bane ___' -- vishaal, 32342's line verbatim. 32343 loses: its line begins only at the adhar.
Cloze on 'Sawan mein ___ mero manva, bhanak suni Hari aavan ki' -- umagyo, 32346's line. 32345 loses: its line is the preceding 'barse badariya' couplet.
Word-gloss of 'adhar' = honth inside 'adhar sudha ras murli raajati', 32343's line, whose description also glosses sudha-ras. 32342 loses: the word-gloss it carries is saanvar, from the face line.

When the jhadi of chhoti-chhoti boondein falls -- the tiny drops are 32348's 'nanhin nanhin boondan mehaa barse', and that image is the only thing distinguishing this stem. 32345 loses: Sawan is named in nearly every pad-2 item, so the season alone cannot be what this one tests.

Which natural event 'daamin dam kai jhar laavan ki' describes -- the lightning flash and the downpour, both halves of 32347's line. 32348 loses: the gentle drizzle and breeze are the picture that follows this one.
In which month the mind fills with umang and harsh -- 'Sawan mein umagyo mero manva' is 32346's line verbatim. 32345 loses: it calls the season man-bhaavan, but the mind's umagna belongs to 32346.

Whom Meera worshipped -- Shri Krishna, the one she petitions directly in the opening vinti, which 32341's description makes the lesson's first question. 32344 loses: its 'bhakt vachhal Gopal' says what he is to devotees, not whom she worships.
When the bhanak of the Lord's coming reaches her -- 32346's own line. 32347 loses: the clouds' gathering is the setting named in the answer, but the tested item is the bhanak.
What Meera's pads rest on -- bhakti to Krishna, i.e. the pad's main subject prem-and-bhakti held by 32341. 32348 loses: its chhaap names the Lord but does not state the pads' subject.
Whom she calls 'bhakt vatsal' -- pad 1's closing line 'bhakt vachhal Gopal', carried by 32344. 32341 loses: it holds the opening vinti, not the closing epithet.

Which alankaar in 'mohani moorati saanvari soorati' -- anupraas, and that line is 32342's own. 32347 loses: it owns the lesson's sound exercise, but for the rain words umad-ghumad, not this face line.

What the vaijayanti maala symbolises -- 32343 is where the maala sits, and its description calls the murli and the maala the two marks by which Krishna is identified. 32344 loses: its symbols are the waist bells and the anklets.
Which quality of Nandlal's eyes enchants her -- their vishaalata and the mohani chhavi, i.e. 32342's 'naina bane vishaal'. 32341 loses: there the eyes are hers, the dwelling she offers.

What 'adhar sudha ras' means -- the amrit-like rasa of the murli at his lips; 32343's description glosses sudha-ras as amrit-ras in so many words. 32342 loses: its description of the face stops at the eyes.
Whom she awaits and why -- Krishna, because she is eager to meet him; 32346 is the line that supplies the pad's reason, the bhanak of his coming. 32345 loses: it names the season, not the expectancy.

Her immediate feeling under the Sawan badariya -- umang in anticipation of Hari's arrival, exactly 32346's umagyo-plus-bhanak pairing. 32345 loses: 'man bhaavan' says the season pleases her; the anticipation is the next line's.
What 'daamin' symbolises -- the momentary flash of lightning, 32347's own image. 32348 loses: it has no lightning, only the drizzle and the cool wind.

Which quality of the accompanying wind attracts her -- its sheetalata and sohaavan pleasantness, 32348's line. 32347 loses: cloud and lightning are its content, and the answer never leaves the breeze.
What sort of songs go with 'Meera ke prabhu Giridhar Nagar' -- aanand-mangal, pad 2's closing line held by 32348. 32344 loses: pad 1's chhaap says santan sukhdaai and contains no singing.

Symbolic weight of the 'kshudra ghantika' at his katitat -- 32344's own line, where the description reaches the waist and the feet. 32343 loses: its ornaments are the murli and the maala, above the waist.
What sound 'noopur shabd rasaal' gives her -- the sweet ring at his feet, the second half of 32344's line. 32343 loses: the sound it carries is the murli's, from the lips.
The Lord's nature towards saints -- 'santan sukhdaai', pad 1's chhaap line under 32344. 32341 loses: the opening vinti asks him into her eyes and says nothing of saints.

What, once seen, gives the mind peace -- the mohak chhavi and its beauty, i.e. 32342's mohini moorat and saanvari soorat. 32341 loses: it is the request to be housed in her eyes, while this asks what the seen form does.
Which month the second poem speaks of -- Sawan, named in 32345's opening line. 32346 loses: it is what Sawan does to her mind, not the naming of the month.

By what names she addresses her prabhu -- 'Nandlal' leads the answer, and that is the vocative of the opening vinti held by 32341. 32344 loses: it supplies only the trailing 'bhakt vachhal Gopal' of the chhaap, the answer's second item.
Meera's kaamana -- that Nand's son dwell in her netra, which is 32341's vinti word for word. 32342 loses: it is the form she goes on to describe, not the wish.
What 'bhanak suni Hari aavan ki' means -- 32346's own line, and its description glosses bhanak as a faint aahat. 32347 loses: the cloud and lightning picture is what she sees, not the hint she hears.
What kind her prabhu is -- sukhdaai to saints and protector of devotees, pad 1's chhaap line under 32344. 32348 loses: pad 2's chhaap names Giridhar Nagar and the mangal songs instead.
To whom both pads are dedicated -- Krishna, the pads' subject of prem and bhakti that 32341 carries. 32344 and 32348 lose: each holds only its own pad's chhaap, while this question spans both.

What she called man-suhaavan -- the badli of nanhin-nanhin drops and the cold wind, 32348's line verbatim. 32345 loses: its 'man bhaavan' is said of the season, while the answer here names the drops and the breeze.
Bhaavaarth of 'mohani moorati saanvari soorati, naina bane vishaal' -- 32342's line in full. 32343 loses: its line starts at the adhar, after this one.

Which roop of Nandlal pad 1 describes -- the answer opens on mohani moorat, saanvari soorat and vishaal netra, 32342's triad. 32343 loses: the murli and maala are the answer's second sentence, an extension of the same sequence.

Explain the bhaav of 'kshudra ghantika katitat sobhit, noopur shabd rasaal' -- 32344's line, and its description names this very line-discussion exercise. 32343 loses: it ends at the chest with the vaijayanti maala.

Sawan's effect on her mind in pad 2 -- the mind fills with umang BECAUSE she hears Hari's aahat, which is 32346's cause-giving line. 32345 loses: it names the season and its pleasingness without the cause.
How nature is drawn in 'daamin dam kai jhar laavan ki' -- lightning flashing and rain falling in sheets, 32347's line. 32348 loses: the still, cool close of the picture is the line that follows.
